title: Wedjat eye-first deepening: can one six-part Eye reconfigure into other glyphs or multiple synthetic sign strings?
research_question: If D011-D016 are treated only as six modern shape primitives, can one Eye be rearranged into other Egyptian signs, and can disjoint subsets form several signs at once strongly enough to motivate a text hypothesis?

critical_distinction.synthetic_glyph: A target Unicode/Gardiner glyph approximated by geometric rearrangement of eye-part masks.
critical_distinction.attested_text: A historically attested Egyptian sign sequence with order, reading, grammar and provenance.
critical_distinction.rule: A synthetic glyph or synthetic glyph sequence is not an attested Egyptian text. Geometry alone supplies neither ordering nor reading.

test_A_shared_scale_one_eye_mode.purpose: Approximate a physical one-eye rearrangement more closely: all six parts preserve their relative natural sizes under one common global scale; each may translate, but no part-specific resize, rotation or mirroring is allowed.
test_A_shared_scale_one_eye_mode.interpretation: When relative piece scale is conserved, the six eye parts do not freely generate the hieroglyphic inventory. The strongest non-source reconstruction is D009, itself an eye/weep sign, and D010 is second. This is more consistent with eye-family morphology than with a general-purpose hidden alphabet.

test_B_free_scale_promiscuity_upper_boun.purpose: Deliberately relax the physical constraint by allowing every part to resize independently. This measures how quickly arbitrary-looking matches appear when degrees of freedom are added.
test_B_free_scale_promiscuity_upper_boun.interpretation: If each eye component is allowed to change scale independently, several unrelated signs become as reconstructible as or more reconstructible than the Wedjat. Therefore flexible visual rearrangement cannot be used to infer hidden text.

test_C_disjoint_same_scale_multi_glyph_p.purpose: Test the strongest version of 'several signs from one eye' without reusing a component: split the six parts into disjoint subsets, preserve one common scale for both targets, and ask whether two or three eye-family glyphs can be approximated simultaneously.

triple_gate_f1_ge_0_30.interpretation: Only weak three-glyph approximations appear after lowering the minimum F1 to 0.30; this is below the preregistered-style moderate visual gate and is treated as noise-level exploratory capacity, not text evidence.

test_C_disjoint_same_scale_multi_glyph_p.critical_semantic_boundary: The surviving pairs are geometric arrangements only. They do not provide sign order, grammatical relation, vocalization, word boundaries or evidence that an Egyptian scribe intended these pairs to be recoverable from a Wedjat.

new_eye_first_model.core: The standardized six-part Eye behaves like a constrained eye-morphology toolkit rather than a freely generative alphabet. Conserving relative scale sharply favors D009/D010 and nearby eye-family signs; relaxing scale produces unrelated false matches.
new_eye_first_model.important_consequence: Future museum-object tests should extract actual eye substructures and preserve their relative scale. Part-specific resizing should be retained only as a negative/false-positive control.

highest_admissible_claim: In this modern Gardiner/Unicode control, one six-part Wedjat can be reconfigured into a small number of other glyph-like arrangements, with the strongest strict shared-scale target being D009 'to weep' and D010 second. Disjoint subsets can approximate a few two-glyph eye-family pairs at moderate similarity, but no three-glyph partition survives F1 >= 0.35. Allowing each part to resize independently greatly increases unrelated matches. Thus the evidence supports limited eye-family reconfiguration capacity, not multiple ancient texts or a hidden message encoded in one Eye.

required: Use SHA-256-sealed isolated museum Wedjat images that pass the v0.7 image-eligibility gate.
Segment actual human-eye core, vertical falcon mark, diagonal falcon mark, spiral/curl and other preregistered substructures from each physical object.
Preserve within-object relative scale; translation-only or rigid transforms are primary.
Test whether D009/D010 eye-family preference replicates across periods and materials.
Use part-specific resizing only as a false-positive upper bound.
Only after a stable cross-object codebook exists, search attested Egyptian corpora for candidate sign sequences; synthetic geometry alone is never called text.
